title: The input request
description: Sends input events to the running sketch. Any number of them can go in one call (a run of them, such as a drag, goes as it is). Placed atomically as ADR-0018 decision 3 requires, and id changes with every request. **A key this version does not read does not fail the request**: it is taken without the key, and the reply's warnings name it — at the top of the request, or inside an event with the event's position (events[0]) — together with the keys that are read, so a misspelt key (buton for button) is never read as the key it resembles. The keys listed here are the whole set, so a writer that adds a key updates this schema first (additionalProperties is false).

id.description: This request's identifier. The reply echoes it back. An id already answered is not processed again, even after the sketch relaunches: the answer left in the reply is the record. Do not reuse an id while the facet remains. **This includes a request that could not be read**: once it is answered, fixing it and placing it again under the same id is not processed — place the fixed request with a new id. **A reply that echoes another id is not yours.** The facet keeps one request and one report, so when another writer places a request over yours, your id may never come back: if `request.json` no longer holds your request and the reply echoes an id that is neither yours nor the one it echoed just before you placed it, your request was either answered and then overwritten, or replaced before it was read. Which of the two cannot be told from the reply.

events.description: The events to send. They are fed in the order they appear. **An unknown type, or an event that cannot be read at all (one without type, or with a value of the wrong type), costs only that one event**: it counts in ignored and the rest still go through. **A request whose id can be read is always answered**: events that are missing, null or not an array count as one in ignored, and nothing is fed. A request whose id cannot be read (missing, not a string, or text that is not JSON) gets no reply, and a request whose id was already answered is not processed again (see id). **A movement or scroll that would make the pointer position, a movement, a drag or a scroll amount overflow a 32-bit float is dropped when it is applied.** A difference overflows once its size passes about 3.4e38, so positions on either side of the canvas more than about 1.7e38 from it are enough (mouseMoved from x = -1.8e38 to x = 1.8e38, even across frames). A frame's total overflows the same way, even from much smaller amounts sent many times (40 scrolled events of dy = 1e37 in one frame: 34 reach the sketch and 6 are dropped). The dropped event still counts in accepted, since whether it overflows depends on the state when it is applied, and the sketch says so once as a warning on standard error. When more events arrive than can be held and the oldest is applied on the spot to make room, it is checked against the totals of the frame before, which have not been reset yet, so an amount around 1e38 can be dropped there that would have fitted at the start of the next frame. A mouseDown or mouseUp is never dropped for its position: its button change is applied and its position is left where it was. Positions outside the canvas that stay finite are applied as they are, not clamped.

items.description: A key not listed here is not read: the event is taken without it (it is not ignored, and the request does not fail), and the reply's warnings name the key with the event's position (events[0]) and the keys that are read. **A field with no meaningful default is required for its type**, and an event missing one counts as unreadable in ignored (the rest still go through). Positions need x and y; keys need code, because 0 is the top left of the surface and the A key, not the absence of a value. button (0 = the left, primary button), dx and dy (0 = no movement), characters (empty) and isRepeat (false) read naturally when left out, so they are optional, and **a null for one of them reads as left out**. A null for a required field (x, y, code) is the same as leaving it out: that one event counts in ignored. mouseMoved says where the pointer went (x and y); mouseMovedBy says how far it moved (dx and dy) without moving the position, which is what the sketch's own window sends while it holds the pointer (requestPointerLock()).

x.description: The canvas coordinate, horizontal. Converting from window coordinates is the sender's job.

button.description: The button. **The macOS button number** (NSEvent.buttonNumber: 0 = left, the primary one; 1 = right; 2 = center), which is a different order from the browser's MouseEvent.button (1 = the middle button, 2 = the secondary one). Buttons past these three, such as back and forward, arrive as their own numbers. On the sketch's own surface this number reads as a `MouseButton`, such as `.right`.

dx.description: For scrolled, how much was scrolled, horizontally; for mouseMovedBy, how far the pointer moved, horizontally, in canvas pixels. **This is for that one event**, and the value reaches the sketch's mouseWheel(deltaX:deltaY:) unchanged (scrolled) or its mouseMoved(deltaX:deltaY:) — mouseDragged(deltaX:deltaY:) while a button is held — and its movedX (mouseMovedBy). mouseMovedBy leaves mouseX and mouseY where they are.

dy.description: How much was scrolled, or how far the pointer moved, vertically. For that one event, as with dx. For mouseMovedBy the vertical axis points down, as the canvas coordinates do.

code.description: The key's code. **A macOS virtual key code** (49 = Space, 0 = A, 126 = up arrow), which is a different system from the codes browsers and Java use. On the sketch's own surface this number reads as a `Key` spelling, such as `.space`. The modifier keys (56 / 60 = left / right Shift, 59 / 62 = Control, 58 / 61 = Option, 55 / 54 = Command) only change which keys are held: they call no keyPressed() or keyReleased() and leave keyCode and key as they were, as the sketch's own window does.

isRepeat.description: Whether this keyDown is the system's key repeat while the key stays held. keyPressed() is called only when a key that is not held goes down, so a repeat reaches keyTyped() alone.
